rulings.challenge_claim: Onset and closing warrant are byte-true at the claimed positions, but a byte-true clause straddles this unit's own cut and is left undisclosed while confidence stands at high with the frontier flag unset.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. The inedibility clause אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹֽעַ (oshb:Jer.24.3, byte tier) stands in this unit's own closing verse, again at 24:2 inside the span, and again in the first verse on the far side of the cut, אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא תֵאָכַ֖לְנָה מֵרֹ֑עַ (oshb:Jer.24.8, byte tier); the two differ only in the accent on the last word, so the recurrence holds at skeleton tier and not at byte tier (sweep: 4 verses -- 24:2, 24:3, 24:8, 29:17 -- three of the four inside this chapter). Neither the boundary rationale nor the device notes reaches it, and the rejected alternative engages continuity only through the word-event form. Cross-seam cohesion binds: a byte-true device straddling a unit's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and the calibration here is high with the frontier flag unset. The seam itself survives: 24:4 opens verse-initially on וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.24.4, byte tier), a member of the narrative word-event shape (sweep: 21 verses at skeleton tier), a tier-1 device that outweighs a descriptive clause whose fourth site at 29:17 shows it to be figure-vocabulary rather than a structural marker. Low is the right weight. One correction to the challenge's own supporting citation: the digit offered for the word-event shape belongs to a five-word string ending in the infinitive of speaking (sweep: 6 verses at skeleton tier), not to the three-word string quoted beside it (sweep: 21 verses) -- a reproduced digit carried on a narrower object than the one named.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes, disclose the inedibility clause as a cross-seam recurrence: name the clause, give its verse count and sites (sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier), and state that it is weighed and does not overturn the word-event seam at 24:4. Then set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true, or argue in boundary_rationale why high survives the disclosed straddle. Cure test: the disclosed clause must carry a digit-bearing count naming its tier, and the calibration fields must be consistent with an acknowledged continuity counterweight -- the test the original failed was cross-seam silence at high confidence.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both items make the same charge: the prose separates the one-site concerning-form header from the eleven-site to-form class correctly, but the declared structured signal carries the class stem with no marker distinguishing the variant, so a one-site object is aggregable into an eleven-site object at exactly the level where the three word-event shapes must stay distinct.
rulings.grounds: Same defect reached independently by both lenses, not two distinct items. The bytes are as the prose states: 25:1 opens verse-initially on הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.25.1, byte tier), ayin-lamed, against the class shape הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.7.1, byte tier), aleph-lamed, and the two objects separate cleanly (sweep: concerning-form header 1 verse; to-form header 11 verses, both at skeleton tier). The declared key is the bare stem the two share, and that stem is itself a blended object: it stands in 12 verses -- the 11 class sites plus 25:1 (sweep: 12 verses at skeleton tier). The hazard is not hypothetical. The same bare stem with no preposition marker is the declared signal on the units headed at 30:1, 40:1 and 44:1, all class members, so as the corpus stands the variant is already indistinguishable from the class under any key-level aggregation, while other class units do carry a preposition-marked key. That live collision, not the prose, carries the severity: medium is right and low understates it.
rulings.remedy: In observed_substrate_signals, replace the bare-stem word-event key with one that marks the variant preposition, following the shape of the preposition-marked key already used on class members; leave boundary_rationale unchanged, its reading being correct. Cure test: aggregate the corpus by word-event signal key and confirm the 25:1 unit no longer falls in the same bucket as the units headed at 30:1, 40:1 and 44:1 -- the test the original failed was key-level indistinguishability from the eleven-verse class.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit registers a closure signal that its own close does not carry: the closing verse carries 0 neum tokens, and the 2 tokens inside the span both sit mid-verse, so the declared signal has nothing in this span's bytes to rest on.
rulings.grounds: The byte facts hold exactly. The close reads וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier) and carries none of the formula -- the 162-verse inventory does not list it -- and the two in-span tokens at 25:9 and 25:12 both sit mid-verse and neither closes anything. What the framing overstates is that the signal has nothing to rest on. It rests on the front seam one verse before the span: 25:7 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.7, byte tier) and 25:8 opens verse-initially on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier), a fresh tier-1 onset -- which is precisely the condition under which the ruled treatment lets that formula do closure work, and it is the pairing the boundary rationale itself names. Corrected finding: not a baseless key but an unscoped one, reading as a claim about this unit's own close where the bytes give nothing. Severity holds at low.
rulings.remedy: Either bind the closure key to the seam it rests on by qualifying it as a front-seam signal, or drop it and let the koh-amar onset key carry the seam alone; in boundary_rationale, state that the closing verse carries no closure formula, so the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8. Cure test: every declared closure signal must be present in the verse it is claimed of -- the test the original failed was a closure key whose only support lies outside the span. For consolidation: this is a corpus_wide_orders candidate rather than a one-unit fix. Ten units declare that closure key and six of them end on a verse carrying none of the 162, and the signal-field contract does not say whether a key may name a device outside the unit's own span; one order should settle the scope question rather than six independent guesses.

rulings.challenge_claim: The no-split ruling at 25:27 rests on an addressee the bytes contradict, and a second frame-command of the same shape stands undisclosed inside the span at 25:28.
rulings.grounds: Both halves verified on bytes. 25:27 opens on וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier), a second-person-singular frame-command directed at the prophet, rendered “You shall tell them” (web:Jer.25.27); the forms addressed to the nations are the plurals inside the quoted speech it introduces, שְׁת֤וּ וְשִׁכְרוּ֙ וּקְי֔וּ וְנִפְל֖וּ (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier). Calling that verse a discourse imperative addressed to the nations collapses the outer frame into its own quoted speech, and the rejected alternative's stated ground -- that the addressee stays the same nations already compelled to drink -- is the part the bytes contest. That is where it bites: a rejected alternative is where the replacement warrant has to hold. The second half holds too. The same frame-command stands again inside the span at וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.25.28, byte tier), unmentioned, so the span carries two rival command seams where the prose weighs one (sweep: 18 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, three of them consecutive here at 25:27, 25:28 and 25:30). The one-unit outcome is not overturned -- command, performance and enforcement still hold together on the ruled symbolic-act rule -- and the closing verse carries a genuine postpositive closure device the unit passes over, נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.25.29, byte tier; sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier). Medium is proportionate: prose and rejected-alternative repair, no boundary change.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale, recut the 25:27 sentence so the frame-command is described as addressed to the prophet and the drinking imperatives as the nations' address inside the quoted speech. In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the addressee ground with the command-and-performance ground that actually carries the one-unit reading, and name the second frame-command at 25:28 as a further rival set aside. In device_notes, record the verse-final closure formula at 25:29 as the close's own corroboration, with its digit and tier. Cure test: every command in the span is read against its verbal form and its addressee before the prose asserts either -- the test the original failed was assigning a second-person-singular frame-command to the plural audience of the speech it introduces.

rulings.challenge_claim: The seam device is asserted through the English alone and labelled with a form-class the pointed bytes do not carry, while the decisive byte fact for this seam (a single-site construction) goes unused.
rulings.grounds: The evidence half is right and stands. The device that opens the unit, וְאַתָּה֙ תִּנָּבֵ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם (oshb:Jer.25.30, byte tier), verse-initial, is nowhere spliced -- both Hebrew splices in the rationale are the poem's content at 25:30b and 25:31 -- so the seam warrant carries no original-language quotation, which a boundary-relevant claim requires. The distinguishing digit does go unused: that verse-initial construction is a single site in the book (sweep: 1 verse at skeleton tier), while the frame-command following it in the same verse is an 18-verse shape standing uncut at 25:27 and 25:28. The label half is over-framed. The verb is prefix-conjugation, the same form standing under a negative at לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte tier) and appearing in 6 verses at skeleton tier, so 'imperative' is not a morphological reading the bytes supply -- but the phrase used is the ruled name of a seam class rather than a bare form assertion, and the command force is byte-supported by the fronted second-person pronoun, by the frame-command that follows in the same verse, and by both witnesses' rendering. Corrected finding: an unspliced seam warrant and an unqualified form word, not a wrong seam; low. Two further defects neither item reaches. The unit declares no signal for its own stated driver while declaring the two devices it expressly refuses to cut on, and the taxonomy already carries a discourse-imperative onset key in use elsewhere in the corpus. And the declared closure key fails here in the same way it fails one unit earlier: the close at 25:33 carries none of the 162 neum verses, and the one verse-final instance in the span, at 25:31, does not close the unit.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale, splice the verse-initial seam construction from 25:30 with its oshb ref and tier named, and either qualify the form word -- command force carried by the fronted pronoun and the following frame-command, not by an imperative form -- or drop the form word; add the single-site digit (sweep: 1 verse at skeleton tier) beside it and state that the 18-verse frame-command shape in the same verse is not the discriminator. In observed_substrate_signals, add a key for the discourse-frame onset the rationale names as the driver, and remove or re-scope the closure key, whose device is absent from the closing verse. Cure test: every device the rationale names as a seam driver appears as a splice with its tier and as a declared signal, and every declared closure signal is present in the verse it is claimed of -- the tests the original failed were an English-only seam warrant and a driver with no signal entry.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item: the opening edge is warranted but the closing edge at 26:6 has no warrant at all, the participant and scene shift opening immediately after being neither cited nor discussed. The other: the unit is cut exactly where its commissioned words are performed and quoted back, with neither the straddling material nor the resulting risk disclosed while confidence stands at high with the frontier flag unset, and the site is named in prose by the other byform.
rulings.grounds: Related but distinct items on one seam; both principal charges hold. The evidence list and the rationale both stop at 26:6, no reference to 26:7 appears in either, and the closing sentence argues only the unit's internal cohesion -- so the close is unwarranted on its face. The straddle is byte-true in two devices. The threat in the closing verse, וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), returns as the charge laid against the prophet at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier): the house phrase is a narrow object (sweep: 6 verses at skeleton tier, half of them in this chapter) and the Shiloh element is per-site, the closing verse's spelling a single site in the book (sweep: 1 verse) against nine for the spelling used across the cut. And the command אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) is reported carried out at אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier). Neither device is disclosed, and the calibration is high with the frontier flag unset. The byform sub-item does not stand: the construction's campaign name covers all three sites in two spellings, and the site's own attested plene form בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלְכ֛וּת (oshb:Jer.26.1, byte tier) is spliced byte-true in the very sentence that uses the class name, against בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte tier) at the other two (sweep: 1 verse and 2 verses at skeleton tier) -- no digit or form claim is left unattested, so there is nothing to cure there. Medium on the principal charges. This seam is shared with the unit opening at 26:7, and the two cures are one edit.
rulings.remedy: Paired seam edit, made once for both sides. In boundary_rationale, add the closing-edge warrant: name the participant and scene change at 26:7 as the ruled seam class that stops this unit at 26:6, and add web:Jer.26.7 to boundary_evidence_refs. In device_notes, disclose the two straddling devices -- the threat quoted back at 26:9 with the per-site Shiloh spellings and their digits, and the command reported performed at 26:8 -- and state that they are weighed as continuity and do not overturn the participant seam. Then set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true. No byform edit is required. Cure test: the closing seam carries a named tier-1 warrant plus a reference to the verse that opens after it, and every device crossing the seam is disclosed with its count and tier -- the tests the original failed were a warrantless close and an undisclosed command-and-quotation straddle at high confidence.

rulings.challenge_claim: The front seam at 26:7 is argued as a clean turn to public narration while two byte-true devices inside the span reach back across it undisclosed, and the boundary is still rated high confidence; the Hebrew engagement offered for the seam is a verb shape that also opens the next seam, so it does not discriminate between the two cuts.
rulings.grounds: The byte facts are right. The completion clause אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier) reports the charge אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) carried out; the threat is quoted back at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier) from וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), the per-site spellings differing (sweep: 1 verse and 9 verses at skeleton tier); and the seam verb וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֛וּ (oshb:Jer.26.7, byte tier) recurs at וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.26.10, byte tier), one of 7 verses at skeleton tier, so it does not by itself separate the two cuts. Two corrections lower the weight. The continuity relation is not wholly unstated: the rationale names this scene as the one where the preceding private instruction is carried out, so what is missing is the byte-level engagement -- no splice, no digit, no weighing -- rather than the relation itself. And the seam is not carried by the verb: the discriminator the unit states is the participant and scene change, a ruled tier-1 class evidenced by a byte-true splice at the seam verse, with the verb as corroboration. What remains is a disclosure gap plus calibration at high confidence on a boundary that does argue both its edges, the far edge through its rejected alternative. Refined to low.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes, disclose the two devices reaching back over the front seam -- the completion clause answering the charge, and the threat quoted back with its per-site spellings and digits -- and state that they are weighed against the participant seam and do not overturn it. Set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true, or argue in boundary_rationale why high survives the disclosed anaphora. This is the same seam as the unit closing at 26:6: make the two disclosures as one paired edit so both sides agree. Cure test: every byte-true device crossing this seam appears once on each side of the pair with a digit and a tier -- the test the original failed was an English-only allusion to the command-and-performance relation carried at high confidence.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closure argument rests on an untiered verbatim-class recurrence claim that the bytes contest: accusation and acquittal share a collocation but neither an order nor an accentuation.
rulings.grounds: Verified. The accusation reads מִשְׁפַּט מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.11, byte tier) and the verdict אֵין לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט מָ֔וֶת (oshb:Jer.26.16, byte tier): the same four words, reordered around the negator, and each of the three accented words differently accented across the two verses -- so the recurrence is not byte-identical, and it is not a contiguous four-word run at skeleton tier either. What does recur is two two-word collocations, the death-sentence pair and the this-man pair, each confined to these two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses apiece at skeleton tier). The rationale's claim that the verdict answers the charge in the very words used to accuse is a recurrence claim carrying no tier label, which the standing rule requires at write time, and the exclusivity that would have sharpened it is available and unclaimed. The echo is real and the boundary is untouched; the defect is one of labelling. Low.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale, replace the very-words wording with a tier-labelled statement: the verdict reuses the accusation's death-sentence and this-man collocations, reordered around the negator, matching at skeleton tier and not at byte tier, each collocation confined to these two verses (sweep: 2 verses each). Cure test: no recurrence claim stands without its tier, and no word-order identity is implied where the bytes reorder -- the test the original failed was an unlabelled verbatim-class claim over a reordered pair.
